candidate.title: PRO-cap
candidate.scope: The middle PRO-cap row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: a four-biotin-NTP nuclear run-on, capped nascent-RNA recovery and repeated streptavidin enrichment, adaptor addition and 5′-end treatment, ending in amplified cDNA representing transcription initiation. The neighboring PRO-seq and CAGE rows and the partial 3′-terminal-structure legend are visible context with no material arrows into this row. They are not additional workflow targets. This describes the depicted implementation, not every implementation of the assay or an executable protocol.

unknowns.question: How are capped and uncapped 5′ ends chemically distinguished during the depicted Antarctic phosphatase/TAP interval? The drawing shows loss of the cap square but neither explicit phosphate groups nor a rejected uncapped-RNA branch, and the supplied primary main text does not expose those supplementary enzyme details. Inspection of the linked primary supplement was attempted, but its PDF URL returned HTTP 404 and the article web view required a browser check; no supplementary content was verified. A readable scoped primary protocol or supplementary fig. S1B is needed to assert the exact selective end chemistry. The cap-loss-to-adaptor route remains interpretable at schematic scope.

checks.rationale: Accept at the declared schematic scope. Independent inspection finds the complete middle PRO-cap route represented by s0-s10, ten distinct local operations and all twenty input/output edges. The four-NTP run-on, extraction without depicted hydrolysis, three distinct bead attachments, intervening recoveries, both adaptor interfaces, cap-loss transition and final cDNA carrier are retained. There are no in-scope splits, pools, discarded-fraction branches or multiple independent substrates compressed into a joint operation. Adjacent rows and the partial chemical legend have no material connection to this route. All six listed paper associations were checked at their actual evidence levels; the sole declared method has primary-paper support for its initiation-site interpretation. The catalogue readout conflict is explicitly resolved without changing the drawn route. Exact phosphate chemistry is left unasserted and does not block this schematic-level account.
